items.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I’ve got some very rare recordings of Pablo Casals. I’ve always liked the way he played Bach and Mozart.

ctx.x: And when we came in today you were playing some classical music, so do you also like the classical we talked about?

Oh sure, “Rites Of Spring”, I can listen to that any day. I’ve got a lot of stuff in the cabinet there, most of my classical music. I’ve got some very rare recordings of Pablo Casals. I’ve always liked the way he played Bach and Mozart. It’s essential to know a little about most of the things that are available in the world; otherwise your education is incomplete. It doesn’t matter what instrument you play. It’s helpful to learn as much as one can just by listening. You learn a lot. Listen to the London…
John Coltrane also, other than his musical influences, his music was also influenced by the events and the culture of this country, for example “Alabama”.
